source: CAMIL GE-V-05 · Page 09 · The Year and Its Parts
notes: The page's four question sentences ('How many days are there in a leap year?') are
excluded: they are phrases, not lexical items.
The two section headers, 'THE DAYS OF THE WEEK' and 'THE MONTHS OF THE YEAR', are full
noun phrases rather than lexical items, so they are reduced to their head nouns 'week'
and 'month' — both essential A1 words that appear nowhere else on the page. 'year' is
still not taught anywhere and is worth adding if a later page does not cover it.
The long time expressions are kept deliberately. 'the day before yesterday' and 'the
night before last' look like phrases, but Spanish has single words for them (antier,
anteanoche, pasado mañana), which is exactly what makes them worth teaching as units of
meaning. At four or five parts they are skipped by dictation automatically.
'fortnight' is chiefly British and a loose fit for quincena, which in Colombia usually
means a pay period. Kept for now; the same profile as 'greenboard' if it should go.
Unit 2 is all twelve months at the twelve-word ceiling, so one month will not get its own
question — the same trade as 'physics' in School subjects. One clean unit reads better
Independence Day and Valentine's Day get generic definitions: Colombia's dates are not
the American ones, so pinning them to July 4th or February 14th would teach a wrong fact.
VERY_EASY: an A1/A2 course, still its early pages.

area.name: The Year and Its Parts
area.description: El calendario completo: los días de la semana, los meses, cómo decir ayer y mañana, y las fiestas del año.

units.name: The days of the week
units.topic: The seven days and the word for the set of them. Note that English writes the days with a capital letter

units.name: The months of the year
units.topic: The twelve months in order, from the start of the year to the end of it

units.name: Weeks, months and years
units.topic: Stretches of time longer than a day: the two days off at the end of a week, the extra day off beside them, and the longer spans. 'fortnight' means two weeks and is mainly British

units.name: Today, yesterday and tomorrow
units.topic: Naming a day by how far it is from today, in both directions. English needs several words where Spanish has one — 'the day before yesterday' is antier and 'the day after tomorrow' is pasado mañana

units.name: Nights, afternoons and the light
units.topic: Naming a part of a day rather than the whole day, and the two moments when the light changes. 'the night before last' is anteanoche

units.name: Holidays and celebrations
units.topic: The days a year is marked by. Describe each one generally, by what it celebrates — never by its date, because Colombia does not keep Independence Day or Valentine's Day on the American dates
